title: Updated Nationally Determined Contribution of the Republic of Tajikistan
organization: Government of the Republic of Tajikistan; UNFCCC repository
temporal_coverage: NDC planning through 2030; cited climate forecasts extend to 2050.
methodology: Government NDC compiles national strategies, sector programs, and stakeholder consultations.
limitations: Government estimates; NDC notes monitoring gaps.

title: Green Transition is Key to Tajikistan’s Economic Revival and Climate Resilience
temporal_coverage: CCDR summary includes projections and investment needs through 2050.
methodology: World Bank Group press-release summary of the Tajikistan Country Climate and Development Report.
limitations: Only the publisher’s release text was inspected; figures and recommendations are not independently re-estimated here.

title: Environment Program in Central Asia
temporal_coverage: RESILAND Tajikistan project status summarized in a 2025 World Bank brief; project launched in November 2022.
methodology: World Bank program brief summarizing country project scope and reported implementation status.
limitations: Publisher summary, not an independent project evaluation; reported outputs are not attributed to climate outcomes.

title: CCRI-DRM Sub-national Tajikistan
temporal_coverage: Subnational child climate and disaster risk model published July 2026; indicator vintages are not stated in the narrative PDF.
methodology: UNICEF's model combines 57 indicators across hazard exposure and child vulnerability for 62 districts.
limitations: Index scores compare districts within Tajikistan; the narrative does not give indicator vintages or detailed component methods.

title: Climate change as a trigger of border river conflicts in Central Asia
temporal_coverage: Article summarizes regional field research conducted in 2021 and a reported April 2021 border confrontation.
methodology: Article summarizes field research in Sughd and regional climate-conflict dialogue.
limitations: Multi-country qualitative summary; no measured climate attribution or causal estimate.

title: The Nexus between Climate Change, Labour Migration, and Radicalisation among Tajik Labour Migrants
organization: Royal United Services Institute and Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung Multinational Development Policy Dialogue
temporal_coverage: RUSI project interviews were conducted March-May 2025; report published 28 November 2025.
methodology: Qualitative scoping study with 80 interviews in Tajikistan, Turkey and remotely.
limitations: Targeted sample, no survey; climate-migration attribution is uncertain and interviewees rarely cited climate directly.

title: Building Resilience Across Tajikistan for a More Inclusive Economy
temporal_coverage: World Bank results summary reports projects and results mainly for 2014-2023, with some operations continuing through 2027.
methodology: Publisher results page summarizes several World Bank-supported programs and reported implementation outputs.
limitations: Results are publisher-reported program outputs; this page does not provide an independent evaluation or isolate climate effects.
